headings.title: Standards for participating on-site wastewater systems

headings.title: Property tax in addition to other taxes

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 7 subsections including subdivisions (1)–(6) of subsection 4 and all notes (L. 1992 H.B. 1307 § 2; Effective 4-7-92), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked municipal wastewater discharge agreements and circuit court enforcement jurisdiction in (1), treatment-cost sharing contracts in (2), refusing noncompliant wastes in (3), O&M and pretreatment powers including $1,000/day industrial-user administrative fines, circuit court actions, and prosecutor referrals in (4), administrative procedural remedy ordinances in (5), knowing false-statement and monitoring-tampering criminal penalties (first and subsequent convictions, supplemental to civil remedies and administrative fines) in (6), and delegated executive officer/designee actions in (7). Retained all 7 drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Amending incorporation decree to operate common public water supply
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1993 H.B. 197 § 1). Permits a chapter 249 sewer district board to petition the circuit court for an amended incorporation decree to construct, maintain, and operate a common public water supply serving ten or more separate properties wholly inside the district outside other political subdivision, chapter 386 certificated water corporation, or chapter 247 water district areas, using initial-formation procedures without a resident vote.

headings.title: Startup deadline and user charges after amended decree
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires beginning operation of acquired existing facilities within ninety days after an amended decree and establishing and collecting user charges in the same manner as sewer rates.

headings.title: Applicability of chapter 249 sewer provisions to water supply
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Applies all applicable chapter 249 provisions to water supply construction, operation, and maintenance in the same manner as sewer facilities.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and history note (L. 1993 H.B. 197 § 1) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked circuit court amended-decree petitions without resident vote for common public water supplies serving ten or more separate properties wholly inside a chapter 249 district outside other political subdivision, chapter 386 certificated, or chapter 247 water district areas in (1), conditional ninety-day startup of acquired existing facilities and sewer-style user charges if the decree is amended in (2), and applicability of chapter 249 sewer provisions to water supply in (3). Revised (2) to "Startup deadline and user charges after amended decree" to preserve the conditional trigger; retained (1) and (3).

headings.title: Eligible cities and counties establishing facility improvement districts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1995 H.B. 88 § 11 subsecs. 1 to 3). Identifies four qualifying city and noncharter first-class county population brackets (including the August 28, 1995 105,000–120,000 county bracket) required to follow subsection 2 procedures to establish a sewage or storm water facility improvement district.

headings.title: Election resolution, notice, cost cap, voting, and ballot form
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including the statutory ballot table and history note. Covers election resolution and notice contents (including optional post-bond annual maintenance assessments and the twenty-five percent cost/bond cap), Mo. Const. Art. VI, § 26 voter approval threshold, separate versus combined ballot rules for non-identical versus identical sewage and storm water boundaries, and the substantial ballot form.

headings.title: Post-election establishment resolution, plans, and cost limitation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes the governing body after requisite voter approval to determine advisability by resolution, establish the district, order preliminary plans and specifications, state required findings including optional post-bond maintenance assessments, and cap assessed costs and bonds at twenty-five percent above estimate without a new election.

Checked the four eligible city and noncharter first-class county population brackets (including the August 28, 1995 105,000–120,000 county bracket) in (1), election resolution, notice, optional post-bond annual maintenance assessments, 25% assessed-cost and bond cap, Mo. Const. Art. VI, § 26 approval percentage, separate vs. single ballot rules for non-identical vs. identical boundaries (retaining source phrasing "sewage water facility improvement district"), and ballot table in (2), and post-election establishment resolution, preliminary plans, findings, and 25% cap without a new election in (3). Retained all 3 drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Mailed assessment notice and lump-sum or installment options
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1995 H.B. 88 § 14 subsecs. 3 to 5). Requires the city or county clerk after adopting the assessment resolution to mail each district property owner parcel descriptions, assigned special assessments, and notice of options to pay in full with accrued interest by a specified date or in subsection 2 annual installments.

headings.title: Annual installments, maintenance assessments, timing, and interest limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers concurrent property-tax assessment in substantially equal annual installments over the section 249.929(2) ballot duration, optional post-bond annual maintenance assessments, first-installment timing, governing-body interest capped at section 108.170 bond limits, and adding accrued interest to the first and subsequent installments.

headings.title: Collection and remittance of assessments to treasurer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Directs that assessments be collected and paid over to the city or county treasurer in the same manner as city or county taxes.
